nb2_lite_1K.texto: A miner in a dust-covered work shirt and drill trousers hangs from a rope tied to a rafter inside an abandoned corrugated-iron shed, his body still, head slumped forward, a wooden crate tipped over on its side beneath his boots. A second miner stands frozen in the open doorway, one hand on the frame, staring at him. Men of European descent with fair to olive skin, dark hair and lean, labour-hardened builds. Derelict mining-camp shed in the Australian outback 1966, rusted iron walls, a broken window, blue-grey tailings dust on the floor. Harsh afternoon sun cutting through gaps in the iron in hard diagonal shafts, the interior in deep shadow. Medium-wide shot, eye-level from the doorway, 35mm lens, moderate depth of field. A grainy 35mm documentary photograph taken in 1966, with muted colors and slight underexposure, in a dark-history realist style. The image has a 16:9 aspect ratio. No readable text, no signage, no labels.
